title: Application of HAADF and DPC to Study Disorder in Transition Aluminas
content: Transition aluminum oxides have complex structures with a high degree of disorder. Presently, there is no theoretical framework that allows to rationalize the extent of disorder in these materials [1, 2]. At the conceptual level, it has been postulated that the disorder is controlled by kinetic factors for low temperature polymorphs, such as γ-Al2O3. On the other hand, in the case of high temperature polymorphs, including δ-Al2O3 and θ-Al2O, the disorder is believed to be controlled by thermodynamic factors. In the current work we study the origin of structural disorder in θ-Al2O3, which is an important polymorph prominently used as catalyst and catalytic support. In a fully ordered state, the structure is isomorphous with β-Ga2O3 but in recent years, it has been shown that the structure accommodates high density of disorder sites leading to a loss periodicity along 2 principal directions [3]. In this work, we present atomic level analysis based on aberration corrected STEM imaging revealing the complexity of θ- and q¢-Al2O3, thus forming the basis for understanding their thermodynamic stability.
